standard_prerequisites.name: Structure of the integral closure of a one-dimensional Noetherian domain
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that B' is a semi-local Dedekind domain.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness criteria for integral extensions and surjectivity of the spectrum map
standard_prerequisites.use: Make the intermediate ring A finite over B and show that A is semi-local.

core_obligations: Record the structural statement that B' is a semi-local Dedekind domain, and fix nonzero x in the Jacobson radical of B' together with y in B' (proof lines 7427-7430).

Consider the subring A generated by B, x and y inside B': show A is finite over B and that, since A and B have the same fraction field, the finite module A/B is supported on the closed points of B, so that a power of the Jacobson radical of B multiplied into A lands in B (proof lines 7430-7436).
Use surjectivity of Spec(B') -> Spec(A) to see that A is semi-local and that x lies in the Jacobson radical m_A of A, with m_A equal to the radical of m_B A (proof lines 7436-7441).
Conclude that x^m y lies in m_B A for some m, hence x^{nm} y lies in B (proof lines 7441-7443).
proof_roadmap: Form the intermediate finite ring generated by the two elements.
Locate the support of A/B at the closed points to absorb a power of the radical.
Show the intermediate ring is semi-local with the same radical behaviour.
Combine the two powers to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that the integral closure B' of a semi-local Noetherian one-dimensional domain B in its fraction field is a semi-local Dedekind domain, and that for a nonzero x in the Jacobson radical of B' and any y in B' some power x^n y lies in B. The proof builds the subring A generated by B, x and y inside B', shows it is finite over B, observes that the finite module A/B is supported on the closed points of B so that a power of the Jacobson radical of B lands in B, notes that Spec(B') -> Spec(A) is surjective and hence A is semi-local with x in its Jacobson radical, and finishes with x^m y in m_B A for some m, giving x^{nm} y in B (proof lines 7427-7443). H2: the intermediate ring A and the two-step use of the conductor to absorb y are the substance.
